tasks.description:
**Question.** Can colour bars be seen to move only when attention tracks them? (Experiment 1.)

**On screen.** A ring around a bull's-eye with a red-green and a luminance grating turning opposite ways. A pointer marks two bars, then leaves; a test pointer appears later.

**The subject.** Fixates the bull's-eye (instructed), tracks the marked bars with attention, and answers yes (J) or no (F): is the test pointer on them?

**Measured.** Tracking accuracy at each luminance contrast ([[param:contrast_min]] to [[param:contrast_max]]).

**Limits.** Colours are matched in luminance per observer, not in cone contrast; needs the rig's photometry.
notes: Paper: 1.0-s pointer, 1.5-s tracking, 240-ms test pointer, 2.0 Hz, 8 cycles, annulus 4.0-8.4 dva, bull's-eye radius 1 dva. ASSUMED: 500-ms bull's-eye period, 500-ms pre-cue, 4-s key deadline, J/F keys, pointer sizes, 4 bull's-eye rings, 500-ms interval.
Target grating (colour or luminance bars) is fixed per session; this file tracks colour bars (configs/task-luminance.yaml tracks luminance bars).
k (equiluminance) comes from the observer's latest equiluminance-speed run; a real session without one is refused.
Field and bar inks: yellow mean #8e7300, red bar #a56800, green bar #707d00 (40% colour contrast); sRGB rendering of the linear gun levels, not a calibrated colour.

Renderer limitation: the guide grammar has no radial (rotating) grating, so the annulus is an angular-layout schematic with short radial strokes at bar centres; the sinusoidal profile and the superimposed luminance grating are not drawn. docs/preview.png is rendered by the task's own scene code and shows the sinusoidal gratings.

tasks.description:
**Question.** At what red-green balance does the colour grating look slowest?

**On screen.** The red-green grating alone, turning in the ring.

**The subject.** Turns a knob on the green-to-red balance until the grating looks slowest; SPACE commits.

**Measured.** The balance setting; its mean is used by every colour task.

**Limits.** An observer- and display-specific setting; it does not calibrate the display.
notes: Paper: minimum apparent speed criterion (p. 1563, note 10). ASSUMED: start range, step, k limits 0.25-4, 60-s limit, 3 settings per direction, 500-ms bull's-eye and interval.
Field and bar inks: yellow mean #8e7300, red bar #a56800, green bar #707d00 (40% colour contrast); sRGB rendering of the linear gun levels, not a calibrated colour.

Renderer limitation: the guide grammar has no radial (rotating) grating, so the annulus is an angular-layout schematic with short radial strokes at bar centres; the sinusoidal profile and the superimposed luminance grating are not drawn. docs/preview.png is rendered by the task's own scene code and shows the sinusoidal gratings.

tasks.description:
**Question.** An alternative equiluminance setting (not the paper's method).

**On screen.** The ring filled uniformly, alternating red-heavy and green-heavy at about [[param:flicker_hz]].

**The subject.** Adjusts the balance until the flicker is least; SPACE commits.

**Measured.** The balance setting.

**Limits.** Can differ from the paper's minimum-speed setting.
notes: Not the paper's method (deviation). 15 Hz, 6 settings, 60-s limit, start range and step are ASSUMED.
The effective rate is refresh/(2 x whole frames per half cycle): 15 Hz at 60 or 120 Hz.
Field and bar inks: yellow mean #8e7300, red bar #a56800, green bar #707d00 (40% colour contrast); sRGB rendering of the linear gun levels, not a calibrated colour.

tasks.description:
**Question.** How much luminance contrast cancels the colour grating's motion?

**On screen.** The colour grating and a luminance grating turning opposite ways.

**The subject.** Without tracking bars, adjusts the luminance contrast until the overall rotation is ambiguous.

**Measured.** The nulling contrast (5-10 % in the paper).

**Limits.** Sets the scale for the tracking task's contrasts.
notes: Paper: motion null without attending to features (p. 1563). Start values, 3% step, limits, 60-s limit and order are ASSUMED.
Field and bar inks: yellow mean #8e7300, red bar #a56800, green bar #707d00 (40% colour contrast); sRGB rendering of the linear gun levels, not a calibrated colour.

tasks.description:
**Question.** How much contrast does a turning grating need to be noticed, alone and under a colour grating?

**On screen.** One grating turning in the ring: luminance alone, luminance under the colour grating, then colour alone.

**The subject.** Adjusts the contrast until the grating is just noticed; SPACE commits.

**Measured.** Threshold per condition, the mean of four settings.

**Limits.** Thresholds near 0.4 % need a 10-bit display.
notes: Paper: four settings per threshold, twice from above and twice from below, luminance alone first. Start values, 5% step, limits and 60-s limit are ASSUMED.
configs/thresholds-direction.yaml runs the direction criterion (luminance cells only); it is a separate parameter set of this task.

Field and bar inks: yellow mean #8e7300, red bar #a56800, green bar #707d00 (40% colour contrast); sRGB rendering of the linear gun levels, not a calibrated colour. Luminance bars: same chromaticity, ±20% (example start contrast).

Renderer limitation: the guide grammar has no radial (rotating) grating, so the annulus is an angular-layout schematic with short radial strokes at bar centres; the sinusoidal profile and the superimposed luminance grating are not drawn. docs/preview.png is rendered by the task's own scene code and shows the sinusoidal gratings.

tasks.description:
**Question.** Does a colour grating's apparent speed drop near equiluminance? (Experiment 2.)

**On screen.** Outer ring: the colour grating at [[param:outer_rate_hz]], with added luminance contrast varying by trial. Inner ring: a luminance grating turning the other way.

**The subject.** Adjusts the inner ring's speed to match the outer ring (this file: overall impression; the tracking file: a pair of tracked bars).

**Measured.** Matched speed at each luminance contrast.

**Limits.** The inner ring's size is ASSUMED.
notes: Paper: 0.5 Hz outer rotation, 15% comparison. ASSUMED: inner ring 1.6-3.6 dva, 8 comparison cycles, the nine luminance levels (read off Fig. 2), photometric zero, start range, step, limits, 120-s limit, 3 matches per level.
Inner-ring bar lines are offset only to keep the schematic readable; phases are random per trial.

Field and bar inks: yellow mean #8e7300, red bar #a56800, green bar #707d00 (40% colour contrast); sRGB rendering of the linear gun levels, not a calibrated colour. Luminance bars: same chromaticity, ±15%.

Renderer limitation: the guide grammar has no radial (rotating) grating, so the annulus is an angular-layout schematic with short radial strokes at bar centres; the sinusoidal profile and the superimposed luminance grating are not drawn. docs/preview.png is rendered by the task's own scene code and shows the sinusoidal gratings.
